content:
Risk appetite is cautious. Managers are still paying for duration and quality, but the latest notes lean less on a soft-landing narrative and more on sticky services inflation and a delayed Fed cut.

Equities. US large-cap growth remains the default overweight in fund letters, with AI capex cited as the earnings support. Several analyst notes flag that leadership is narrower than last month: mega-cap tech still leads, but breadth in cyclicals has faded.

Rates and credit. Newsletters treat the front end as range-bound. Investment-grade spreads are described as tight versus history; one licensed fund letter prefers up-in-quality credit over adding duration.

Asia. HK and China property commentary is still defensive. A call transcript on regional banks stressed liquidity over growth. Gold and USD cash show up as the common hedge across internal notes.

Versus last overview. Sentiment is slightly more defensive than the previous summary: fewer letters argue for adding beta, and more sources put a higher weight on a late-cycle credit event than on a re-acceleration in global PMIs.
